step1_figure.circuit_type: Common-Source Amplifier with Current Source Load
step1_figure.description: The circuit is an NMOS common-source amplifier (M1) loaded by a PMOS current source load (M2) biased via a wide-swing bias generator (SUB_1 providing Vbias1), with AC coupling, 100k source resistance, and Miller capacitance shown in Fig 21.20 (page 674).

quiescent_bias_current.description: DC bias current conducted by the output branch under saturation (Class A operation)

equation.explanation: M2 acts as a current source biased by the bias generator to provide the quiescent branch current.
equation.assumptions: Both M1 and M2 operate in the saturation region.

sky130_expected.calculation: Nominal reference current from bias circuit is designed for 20 uA. At VDD = 1.8 V, I_D ~ 20 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard bias current tracking across corners and VDD variations in Sky130.

quiescent_power.description: Total static DC power consumption of the amplifier and bias circuitry

equation.explanation: Total power drawn from the 1.8V rail by the amplifier core and bias circuit branches.
equation.assumptions: All branches operating at their static bias points.

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD = 1.8 V; amplifier branch conducts ~20 uA, bias generator conducts ~100-150 uA total; P_DC ~ 1.8 V * 150 uA = 270 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sum of quiescent currents in the amplifier branch and current reference branches.

equation.explanation: Small-signal gain is given by the input transconductance multiplied by the parallel output resistance of M1 and M2.
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 are in saturation; lambda_n = lambda_p = 0.1 V^-1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical intrinsic gain of Sky130 long/medium-channel devices under modest inversion.

open_circuit_gain.description: Intrinsic maximum single-transistor open-circuit gain of M1

equation.explanation: Maximum attainable gain when load resistance is infinitely large.
equation.assumptions: M1 in saturation loaded by an ideal current source.

sky130_expected.calculation: A_open = gm1 * ro1 = 328 uA/V * 500 kOhm = 164 V/V = 44.3 dB (6 dB higher than Av loaded with ro2).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Twice the output impedance of the ro1||ro2 case.

slew_rate.description: Maximum charging rate of the output capacitive load

equation.explanation: Limited by the maximum current sourced by M2 (20 uA) into the load capacitance (1 pF).
equation.assumptions: Input steps negative, fully shutting M1 off so all 20 uA charges the load capacitor.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Defined directly by current source M2 output capability into a 1 pF load.

input_pole_fin.description: Dominant input corner frequency due to Miller-multiplied capacitance

equation.explanation: Pole caused by source resistance Rs charging input Miller capacitance.

sky130_expected.calculation: Cin,Miller ~ 1 pF * (1 + 50) = 51 pF. fin = 1 / (2 * pi * 51 pF * 100 kOhm) = 31.2 kHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by the 100k source resistance and 1pF Miller compensation capacitor.

equation.explanation: Zero created by feedforward through the gate-drain/Miller capacitor Cgd1.
equation.assumptions: Cgd1 is dominated by Cc = 1 pF.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Set by M1 transconductance and 1 pF compensation capacitance.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency where the voltage gain drops to 0 dB (unity gain)

equation.explanation: Gain-bandwidth product roll-off frequency given dominant pole behavior.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by source resistance Rs and Cc.

step3_testbench.description: SPICE testbench to verify common-source amplifier performance: DC operating point, AC transfer function (low-frequency gain, fin, fz, fun), and transient slew rate with a step input.
